text: Isolated effect of each assumption on GOP

runs.text: To identify the main drivers, each assumption was changed on its own while the other three were held at the expected-case value:
Greatest effects on GOP: occupancy and ADR.

Occupancy has the largest effect because every lost room-night removes SAR 342 of contribution (ADR SAR 430 less SAR 88 variable cost), a contribution margin ratio of about 80%. One percentage point of occupancy equals 42 room-nights, or roughly SAR 14,364 of GOP. ADR is a very close second because a price reduction saves no cost at all: every riyal discounted is lost directly from profit, and it applies to all 2,856 room-nights (about SAR 2,856 of GOP per SAR 1 of ADR). By comparison, F&B has a much lower contribution margin (SAR 43 per cover, about 44%), so changes in covers hurt less, although the average check still matters because, like ADR, it falls straight to profit.

The comparison also shows operating leverage. Fixed costs total SAR 598,000 (135,000 + 148,000 + 315,000). Because these do not fall when demand falls, a 12.9% drop in total revenue (SAR 260,250) produces a 28.6% drop in GOP. The Rooms department is the hotel’s profit engine, contributing over 80% of Total Departmental Income in both scenarios.
I recommend that management adopt the expected case as the main revenue target, but set spending and staffing on the conservative case, with the gap acting as a flexible-budget buffer.

The expected case is built on mid-range, internally consistent assumptions, so it is a fair and motivating target for the sales and revenue teams. Using only the conservative case as the target could lead to under-selling, and managers might release discounted rates too early. On the other hand, the GOP gap of more than SAR 209,000 is too large to ignore. If management staffs and purchases for 68% occupancy and the month turns out closer to 63%, labour hours, food purchases and discretionary spending would be committed before revenue arrives.

In practice, the hybrid plan means: (1) revenue targets of SAR 1,228,080 for Rooms and SAR 795,400 for F&B; (2) the core rota and food purchasing planned for the conservative volumes (2,646 room-nights and 7,600 covers), with on-call staff and short-lead purchasing added only when pickup confirms higher demand; and (3) discretionary undistributed spending, such as marketing campaigns or minor repairs, released in stages once mid-month results are known. Because the variable costs per room (SAR 88) and per cover (SAR 54) are known, the budget can be flexed to the actual volume at month-end, so managers are evaluated against the costs that should have been incurred at the level of activity actually achieved. Even in the conservative case the hotel still earns a GOP of SAR 521,982, so the downside is manageable and does not justify an overly defensive plan.
